title: Redis Cluster Architecture
description: Understand how Redis Cluster distributes data across multiple nodes using hash slots and master-replica architecture.

data.text: Redis Cluster is a distributed implementation of Redis that automatically shards your data across multiple nodes. Unlike Redis Sentinel, which only provides high availability for a single master, Redis Cluster partitions the entire dataset so that no single node holds all the data. This enables horizontal scaling for high-throughput workloads.
Hash Slots: The Core Partitioning Mechanism

Redis Cluster divides the entire keyspace into 16,384 hash slots. Every key is assigned to exactly one slot using the CRC16 algorithm modulo 16,384. Each master node in the cluster owns a subset of these slots. When you write or read a key, the client computes which slot it belongs to and routes the request to the responsible master.

data.title: Why Hash Slots?
data.text: Using 16,384 fixed slots means adding or removing nodes only requires redistributing slots — not rehashing the entire dataset. This makes cluster resizing relatively fast and predictable.

data.text: Each master can have one or more replicas. If a master fails, one of its replicas is automatically promoted to master by the cluster's voting mechanism. A quorum of the majority of master nodes must agree on a failure before promotion occurs, preventing split-brain scenarios.

items.question: Can Redis Cluster store more data than a single Redis instance?
items.answer: Yes. Since data is sharded across multiple masters, you can scale your dataset horizontally. Each master still has a memory limit, but the aggregate capacity grows with each added node.

items.question: What happens if two nodes lose connectivity?
items.answer: If a minority of masters become partitioned, those nodes enter an error state and reject writes. Clients must be configured to redirect to reachable nodes. A minority partition continues serving its slots normally.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Redis Cluster uses 16,384 hash slots to partition data across master nodes
Keys are assigned to slots using CRC16(key) mod 16384
Each master should have at least one replica for high availability
Multi-key operations are only allowed when all keys are in the same hash slot
data.takeaway: Redis Cluster enables horizontal scaling of Redis by sharding data across multiple nodes, but requires understanding hash slots to design keys effectively.
